findings.diagnosis: 4.9's retention limb keeps recurrence that is deliberate, and a section of boundaries stated as a litany is the clearest case of it. Restating the subject in the second item breaks the run. And it is not, finally, proven is the last and heaviest item in the litany, and finally marks it as the arrival. Compressing it to a lead-in clause removes both the position and the sentence in which the book undertakes not to pretend otherwise.

findings.diagnosis: In the open and publishes honestly are the transparency terms of the commitment CTD-0052 tracks, and removing them narrows an unbacked promise by attrition rather than by decision. The item's remedy is to back the promise or recast it explicitly as a proposed research norm, not to let it erode. Not deployment is also the reader's assumption about what a project of this kind does first, and at all is the concession that the signature may not exist.

findings.summary: Two antitheses were flattened into their positive halves.

evidence.baseline: the kind arrived at by observation, the noticing that life organizes through relationship, not the kind demanded by doctrine ... Its measure of success is not the absence of trouble but the presence of the capacity to recover from it
evidence.shipped: The reverence described in the Soil comes from observing that life organizes through relationship, not from doctrine ... Success means the capacity to recover from trouble, not the absence of trouble

findings.diagnosis: Arrived at and demanded are the two verbs the distinction rests on: observation arrives at reverence, doctrine demands it, and reducing both to prepositional phrases loses the difference in what each does to a person. Absence and presence are a matched pair and the sentence turns on the substitution of one for the other. The revision keeps the terms and drops the symmetry that makes them an argument.

text: It would be easy, having come this far, to mistake what has been described for something it is not. So let the boundaries be drawn plainly, because a thing is known as much by what it refuses as by what it reaches for.
Providence is not a government. It governs no one, holds no monopoly on force, and grants itself no authority a person cannot revoke by walking away.

It is not a religion, though it touches reverence. It asks for no belief. The reverence it points toward, as the Soil showed, is the kind arrived at by observation: the noticing that life organizes through relationship. It is not the kind demanded by doctrine.
It is not a company that owns you, and not a platform that harvests you. There is no central store of your life to be sold, because the architecture refuses to build one.

It is not a utopia. It assumes conflict, failure, self-interest, and harm, and is designed for repair rather than perfection. Its measure of success is not the absence of trouble but the presence of the capacity to recover from it.
And it is not, finally, proven. This is the most important boundary of all, and the book will not pretend otherwise.

The entire architecture rests on a single empirical claim: that the quality of genuine human presence can be detected reliably, non-invasively, and in a way that is hard to counterfeit. If that claim is false, Providence is not dangerous. It is simply hollow. There is no currency, no membrane, no trust that travels. Only a beautiful idea resting on nothing.

So the honest order of operations is not to build the cathedral and hope. It is to test the foundation first, in the open, before the weight goes on it. The first real work of this project is not deployment. It is a study: adversarial, independent, willing to fail. It asks whether presence leaves a real signature at all, and publishes honestly what the instruments can and cannot see. If it can be measured, the rest becomes worth building. If it cannot, the most valuable thing the experiment can do is say so clearly, and save a generation of builders the trouble.
This is what it means to call the thesis falsifiable rather than merely hopeful. It names the exact place it could be wrong, and agrees to look there first.

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. The ledger was searched before restoring. Two items name passages here and both are unresolved, which changed no disposition but did change the reasoning: the restorations are recorded as holding open decisions rather than as preferences about wording.

R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Five em dashes. Two introduced a specification and became colons. One separated a landing from the triad before it and became a period, leaving Only a beautiful idea resting on nothing to stand alone. Two fenced material with internal commas and the syntax was rewritten.

The pass's attachment of the detection adverbs directly to the verb, reliably, non-invasively, and in a way that is hard to counterfeit. The em dash there was fencing an adverbial that reads cleanly attached, and a colon before adverbs would be punctuation theater.
The pass's split of the study sentence at the relative clause, which the colon repair required independently.

The renamed heading, Boundaries and Burden of Proof, under the volume ruling on renames. Recorded with the other heading questions: the baseline heading names the section's own structure, a list of what the work is not, and the replacement names its topic.

The opening and its governing aphorism, the it is not litany across four items with its culminating and finally, the not dangerous but hollow distinction, both antitheses, the transparency terms of the study commitment, the repeated no in the currency triad, and the hyphen in non-invasively.

openQuestions: Heading decision 5 of 5. Keep Boundaries and Burden of Proof, or restore What This Is, and What It Is Not? The current heading names the topic. The earlier heading names the section's structure, a litany of denials that the opening paragraph justifies as a way of knowing a thing. Restoring it costs a reviewed route alias.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the volume-01 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. Sixteenth consecutive section to need none. F2 is the volume's first confirmed repetition of an identical finding across two sections, which retroactively strengthens the earlier record: what looked like one editor's judgment about one sentence was a habit applied wherever the construction appeared. F4 is the more useful case for the method, because it shows R-LEDGER-WINS working in the direction opposite to its first use. There the ledger overruled a restoration; here it requires one, because an open promise weakened without a decision is a debt item closed by attrition.

This audit is the section's evidence under the current standard; the original title is a historical fact and is not rewritten.

substitutionTest.method: Surviving baseline sentences were counted before any pairing test. A sentence counts as surviving only when it appears character-exact in the shipped section after whitespace and typographic-quote normalization, so an authorized punctuation repair counts as non-surviving. The count is a floor on fidelity, not a judgment of it.
